newsitem.title: UK: BSkyB rebounds on digital TV hopes.
newsitem.headline: BSkyB rebounds on digital TV hopes.

text.p: Shares in British Sky Broadcasting Group Plc were the biggest percentage gainers in the FTSE 100 index at midday on Tuesday, amid renewed hopes for the company's digital television plans, dealers said.
Rebounding from a three-month low of 559p set on May 2, the stock was up 26-1/2p or 4.7 percent at 593-1/2 by 1126 GMT in moderate trade of 1.9 million shares.
Dealers said there was also renewed talk that Japan's Matsushita, a partner in launching the new interactive digital service, could also be interested in taking a stake in BSkyB itself.

Earlier a report in the Financial Times said BSkyB would on Wednesday announce plans for 200 digital television channels in the UK, combining interactive services such as home banking, shopping and the Internet.
The newspaper said BSkyB had finalised details of a 700 million pound joint venture with British Telecommunications, Midland Bank and Matsushita to form British Interactive Broadcasting (BIB).
Carlo Campomagnani, analyst at Lehman Brothers, said digital TV could provide an important revenue stream for BSkyB though he remained cautious on the stock.
"Digital services especially pay-per-view could potentiall bring in a highly profitably stream of new business to the company," Campomagnani said.

"The issue that has to be faced is the cost of the set top boxes -- which is very high at the beginning -- who is going to fund them and how much BSkyB will contibute... we believe pay-per-view is an important piece of the BSkyB puzzle but we also believe the good news is discounted and the stock is expensive."
The Lehman analyst said he retained an "underperform" rating on BSkyB shares.
The FT said the function of the BIB consortium would be to provide heavy subsidies for the digital decoders, which consumers would need to receive the new services.
These would initially retail at a discounted 200 stg each to get the boxes and associated services on to the market, the FT said.
